recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is recommended unless a future terminology publication process changes the canonical message-significance-category artifact outside the current core source.
issue_request: FHIR-15107 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Conformance change request for STU3 asking that message-significance-category codes Consequence, Currency, and Notification be changed to lowercase consequence, currency, and notification.
initial_application: Jira comments cite svn revision 13571, and git history contains 0396ead17e3f9b40a54b1f2ee25ca882474e34f5, "GF#15107 - fix case of codes", which changed the old capabilitystatement spreadsheet rows from uppercase to lowercase. Later source refactoring moved this terminology into source/messagedefinition without reintroducing uppercase code values.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists messagedefinition=MessageDefinition and assigns it to the INM work group, putting the inspected files in current build scope. The current CodeSystem uses lowercase code values with capitalized displays, MessageDefinition.category is required-bound to the ValueSet with lowercase short text, and current examples use lowercase category values. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community or minutes evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is needed: the current active source already implements the requested lowercase codes and current-source grep found no uppercase MessageDefinition category/code values.
